# UI Design Library

> 3,805 free copy-paste HTML+CSS UI elements (buttons, loaders, cards, forms, toggles, inputs, checkboxes, patterns, radio buttons, tooltips, notifications) from Uiverse.io, MIT licensed. Every element is pure HTML + CSS, no JavaScript, no login, no account, no API key. Browse, copy the code, paste it into your project, keep the author credit.

> Live site: https://mr-10.github.io/ui-design-library
> Data version: ad0a23a75570

## Categories

- buttons: 1232 elements
- loaders: 718 elements
- cards: 726 elements
- toggle-switches: 260 elements
- inputs: 226 elements
- forms: 181 elements
- checkboxes: 172 elements
- patterns: 103 elements
- radio-buttons: 102 elements
- tooltips: 62 elements
- notifications: 23 elements

## Machine-readable data

For SEARCH, prefer the small per-category files (id, name, one-line description, trigger, top 4 tags) or the MCP server below — do not download the full index just to search:
- Per-category search file: https://mr-10.github.io/ui-design-library/data/search/<category>.min.json (e.g. buttons, loaders, cards, forms, inputs, checkboxes, toggle-switches, patterns, radio-buttons, tooltips, notifications)
- Full index (id, name, category, trigger, tags, description) — only when you need the whole list at once: https://mr-10.github.io/ui-design-library/data/index.min.json
- Categories (names and counts): https://mr-10.github.io/ui-design-library/data/categories.json
- One element (metadata, html, css, combined single-file version): https://mr-10.github.io/ui-design-library/api/<category>/<id>.json
- Element source on GitHub: https://github.com/mr-10/ui-design-library/tree/main/uiverse/<category>/<id>

## Use with AI agents (MCP)

An MCP server is available as the npm package `ui-design-library-mcp` (command `npx -y ui-design-library-mcp`). It exposes search_elements, list_categories, get_element, get_similar and get_random over this data. See the README section "Use with AI agents" for the config for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf.

## Rules for using an element

- Use at most one element's code per answer; search first, then fetch that one element.
- Keep the author credit (author name + uiverse.io source link).
- Adapt colours to the project; keep the element's behaviour.
